d11_2025_td2_q4_expl:
r1 corresponds to the selection of lines (restrict) from the table iin_vols by keeping only those for which the attribute arrivee is equal to 'Nice'. r2 corresponds to a projection (proj) of the column pilote. r2 is then the list of pilot numbers for pilots having never made a flight to Nice.
r3 corresponds to a selection of lines (restrict) in the table iin_pilotes by keeping those for which the attribute npilote does not belong to the list r2. r4 corresponds to a projection (proj) of the attribute nom. r4 then containsthe list of pilot names who does not belong to r2.
Said differently, the request returns the names of pilots having never made a flight towards Nice as a main pilot (no copilot).
d11_2025_td2_q5_expl:
r1 corresponds to a selection of lines (restrict) in the table iin_avions for which the attribute capacite is strictly inferior to 300. r2 corresponds to a projection (proj) of the column navion. r2 then contains the planes numbers of planes whose capacity is inferior to 300.
r3 corresponds to a selection of lines (restrict) from the table iin_vols for which the attribute navion belongs to the list r2. r4 corresponds to a projection (proj) of the colomn arrivee. r4 then contains the destinations for which the plane does not belongs to the list r2.
Said differently, the request returns the destinations of flights made on a plane whose capacity is superior of equel to 300.
d11_2025_td2_q6_expl:
r1 corresponds to a projection (proj) of the columns arrivee and depart from the table iin_vols. It is thus all the return flights.
r2 corresponds to a selection of lines (restrict) in the table iin_vols for which the couples (depart, arrivee) belongs to the list r1. r3 corresponds to a projection of the columns depart and arrivee. It is then the flights belonging to the list of flights r1.
Said differently, the request returns the couples of cities for which there exists a return flight.

d11_2025_td6_title: 📖💻 TD/TP 6 : Database definition language and update
d11_2025_td6_description:
In the following, you will create the tables mesvillages and mesgaulois which will be copies of the tables villages and gaulois, with all integrity constraints. The table structures are the following :

village(vilno, nom, nbhutte, chef)
  • vilno : village number (number on two figits), must be given a value
  • nom : name (string of maximum 20 characters), must be given a value
  • nbhutte : number of huts (number on three digits)
  • chef : number of the village chief, references gauno of gaulois
  • vilno : village number (number on two digits), must be given a value

gaulois(gauno, nom, sexe, metier, vilno)
  • gauno : Gaul number (number on three digits), must be given a value
  • nom : name (string of maximum 15 characters), must be given a value
  • sexe : sex (string exactly 1 character), can only be 'M', 'F' or NULL
  • metier : job (string of maximum 15 characters)
  • vilno : village number where the Gaul inhabits, references vilno of village

Given this description, these two tables have crossed referencies.
Note : we use these naming conventions for the constraints
  • primary key : pk_tablename
  • foreign key : fk_sourcetablename_sourcecolumnname
  • applicative constraint : c_tablename_columnsnames
  • unicity constraint : u_tablename_columnsnames
d11_2025_td6_ldd: Database definition language - mesgaulois and mesvillages tables
d11_2025_td6_q1: The type of the column chef in the table village is not described, can we guess it ?
d11_2025_td6_q1_rep: Yes, it must be the same as the referenced column, gauno from gaulois.
d11_2025_td6_q2: Let's suppose that we create the table mesvillages first, can we create it with the reference constraint of chef to gauno from mesgaulois ?
d11_2025_td6_q2_rep: No because it is not possible to reference a column which does not exist yet. We must first create mesvillages without the reference constraint, then create the table mesgaulois with the reference constraint vilno to vilno from village because the column exists, then add the reference constraint of chef to gauno from gaulois using an alter table command.
d11_2025_td6_q3: What is the difference between CHECK(sexe IN ('M', 'F') or sexe is NULL) and CHECK(upper(sexe) IN ('M', 'F') or sexe is NULL) ?
d11_2025_td6_q3_rep: sexe IN ('M', 'F') forces the input to be in upper case, upper(sexe) allows both upper and lower cases in the table.

d11_2025_td6_q17:
Add to the table table mesbatailles the following constraint.
ALTER TABLE mesbatailles ADD (CONSTRAINT c_mesbatailles_datebat CHECK(datebat < sysdate));
What happened ?

This constraint should have the role of verifying that the battle date is prior to the current date. This is not allowed because once a constraint has been verified, it must remain valid. (Instead, the current date changes every day so the condition could evolve and become false in the future).
